title: "Data & reproduction"

---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("_data.R")
sz <- function(f) sprintf("%.1f MB", file.size(file.path(SITE, f)) / 1e6)
```

## Downloads (data version `r VERSION$baseline_version`)

| File | What it is | Size |
|---|---|---:|
| [manifesto_scores_v2026a.csv](data/download/manifesto_scores_v2026a.csv) · [.parquet](data/download/manifesto_scores_v2026a.parquet) | One row per manifesto: identifiers, the combined scores used in the paper, each model's scores, the number of models per dimension and the model provenance. | `r sz("data/download/manifesto_scores_v2026a.parquet")` |
| [evidence_poplib_v4_v2026a.parquet](data/download/evidence_poplib_v4_v2026a.parquet) | One row per chunk, model and dimension: score, evidence status, the first 8 words of the quote, and whether the chunk counted in the score. | `r sz("data/download/evidence_poplib_v4_v2026a.parquet")` |

Scores and evidence flags: [CC-BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); please cite
the paper and the data (below). The manifesto texts are © their authors and distributed by the
[Manifesto Project (WZB)](https://manifesto-project.wzb.eu/); obtain them there with the
manifesto id (`doc_id` = CMP party code _ election year and month). This site does not
redistribute them, and quotes are cut to 8 words.

```r
library(arrow)
scores <- read_parquet("https://populism-llm.org/data/download/manifesto_scores_v2026a.parquet")
# populism_overall, liberalism_overall, lib_political, lib_social, lib_economic,
# lib_financial_market, pop_ideology_direction (-1 left .. +1 right), ...
fixest::feols(liberalism_overall ~ populism_overall | countryname + year, scores, cluster = ~party)
```

The last line is the paper's headline regression (column 1 of Table 4).

The exact system prompt, user message and output schema sent to the models are exported from the
scoring code with every build: [system prompt](data/prompt/system_prompt_poplib_v4_elements.txt),
[user message](data/prompt/user_prompt_poplib_v4.txt),
[schema](data/prompt/schema_poplib_v4.json) (see [methodology](methodology.qmd#the-exact-prompt)).

## Columns

- `doc_id`, `countryname`, `partyname`, `partyabbrev`, `parfam` (party family label), `party`
  (CMP party code), `date`, `year`, `token_count`.
- Thirteen dimensions, 0–10, combined across models: `pop_anti_elitism`, `pop_people_centrism`,
  `pop_manichean`, `populism_overall`, `pop_ideology_left`, `pop_ideology_right`,
  `pop_ideology_centrist`, `pop_ideology_overall`, `lib_political`, `lib_social`, `lib_economic`,
  `lib_financial_market`, `liberalism_overall`. The same with suffix `_sonnet`, `_gpt41mini`,
  `_gemini` for each model, and `n_models_<dim>`.
- `pop_ideology_direction` = (right − left) / (right + left + centrist); the variants `_zero`,
  `_ge2`, `_all3` handle missing components differently (robustness).
- Provenance: `endpoint_<model>`, `resolved_<model>`, `share_logged_<model>`, `aggregation`,
  `validation_rule`, `baseline_version`, `corpus_version`.

CMP coding variables (such as `rile`) are not included; they are available from the Manifesto
Project.

## Reproduction

The paper's numbers come from one replication chain. It reruns every table and figure from the
model output and checks each output file against a recorded checksum. The replication package
(code, redacted model output, documentation) will be published with the paper; until then,
please contact [Sebastian Stöckl](mailto:sebastian.stoeckl@uni.li).

This site is built from the same chain: it recomputes all scores from the public model output and
refuses to build if any score differs from the chain's value.
